title: Mitigate variant‑affinity misassignment causing route oscillation and cross‑region capacity thrash
creator: Priya Nair
description: Summary: During a capacity pressure event on 2025-11-05 the smart-routing service began misassigning variant affinity scores for a subset of long‑running customer traffic. The misassignment caused sticky affinity to prefer an undersized regional variant, which then triggered throttles and cross‑region reroutes. The reroutes and repeated fallback attempts produced oscillatory behaviour (route thrash) that amplified capacity burn and led to increased 5xx rates for affected customers for ~27 minutes. Root causes identified: (1) an off‑by‑one regression in affinity decay logic that prevented timely evictions of stale per‑route affinity state, (2) stale topology cache TTL mismatch between router and policy engine, and (3) circuit‑breaker backpressure thresholds that were too permissive and allowed repeated variant failovers instead of tripping to a safety fallback.
timeline: 2025-11-05 14:12 UTC — First alerts: elevated 5xx rates and latency spikes for serving-region eu-west-1. Pager triggered for Routing-Pager duty.

2025-11-05 14:15 UTC — On-call rotated to Priya Nair and Marco Luis. Initial mitigation: increased variant capacity weight for healthy North America pool to accept rerouted traffic; partial relief observed.
2025-11-05 14:27 UTC — Observed oscillation: requests repeatedly moved between eu-west-1 undersized variant and na-1 fallback; traffic churn increased GPU utilization by 32% in NA region.

2025-11-05 14:40 UTC — Hotfix deployed: disabled affinity persistence for affected route tag and tightened circuit-breaker threshold to immediate fallback after 2 failover attempts (rolled out to 50% of routers).
2025-11-05 14:50 UTC — System stabilized; alerts subsided by 14:58 UTC. Post-incident page created and triage started.
2025-11-06 — Root cause analysis session with Serving Runtime, Router, and Policy teams. Identified code regression (PR #4521) and a config drift in cache TTLs between services.

2025-11-07 — Patch PR #4587 opened to fix decay algorithm and add unit tests for affinity eviction. Telemetry dashboard added to surface per-route affinity age distribution (ticket ENG-21001-telemetry).
2025-11-10 — Load test of patched logic in staging with synthetic churn workload; observed stable routing and immediate fallback when variant fails.
2025-11-12 — This ticket created to track follow-ups, implementation, testing, and rollout plan for production-safe hardening.
action_items: Fix: revert off-by-one in affinity decay window and add deterministic unit + property tests (owner: Ava Chen, PR #4587).
Config: align topology cache TTL across Router and Policy Engine; add config validation at startup to warn on mismatch (owner: Marco Luis).
Safety: implement a fast‑path circuit breaker that trips to a global safe-variant after 2 failovers for a given route key (owner: Systems).
Telemetry: surface per-route affinity age and failover counts in Console with alert thresholds (owner: Observability).
Runbook: add explicit steps to force affinity eviction and manual fallback for on-call; add a pre-scripted throttling playbook (owner: SRE).
Simulation: add regression test in chaos lab that injects slow variant degradation and verifies fallback convergence within 30s (owner: QA).
Release plan: staged rollout in three waves (5%, 25%, 100%) with canary monitoring for failover count delta and 5xx regression windows (owner: Release Eng).
Retro + lessons: schedule a cross-team retro and update routing design doc to include invariants about affinity TTL and backpressure hysteresis (owner: Product).

Related tickets: ENG-31245 (sticky-route-state-after-capacity-failover) — investigate overlap in affinity state retention behavior; ENG-41207 (inconsistent-variant-tagging) — confirm variant tagging fingerprints are unique across regions.
Risk: changing circuit-breaker sensitivity may increase false-positive fallbacks during transient network blips; mitigation: short observation window + configurable thresholds per customer tier.
Success criteria: no routing oscillation observed under the staged chaos test and production failover counts reduced by >= 90% for affected routes in the first week after rollout.
